Case Studies - Real Results from AICORE Projects

Explore AICORE Technologies case studies - real-world deployments of AI, IoT, automation, and embedded systems delivering measurable results for clients.

Anonymised — Manufacturing Sector: A mid-size manufacturing facility was experiencing an average of 14 hours of unplanned machine downtime per month across its production lines. The root cause was almost always predictable — bearing wear, motor temperature drift, or pneumatic pressure loss — but without real-time sensor data, failures were only discovered when machines stopped. Maintenance was reactive and expensive, with emergency call-outs costing 3–5x more than scheduled servicing.

Anonymised — Logistics & Distribution Sector: A distribution company handling fast-moving consumer goods across Lagos and Abuja had no reliable method for tracking stock movements between its two warehouses. Inventory counts were done weekly by hand, reconciliation took two days, and discrepancies of 5–15% were common. The business could not reliably promise delivery timelines because it had no real-time visibility into what was physically on hand versus what the spreadsheet said.

Secondary School — Lagos State: A private secondary school in Lagos wanted to introduce a practical technology programme that went beyond computing theory. The school had no existing robotics or electronics equipment, no teachers with embedded systems experience, and a tight budget constraint. The programme needed to be deliverable within an existing timetable slot without requiring additional staff.

Anonymised — Commercial Solar Operator: A commercial solar installation company managing systems across 30+ client sites had no centralised visibility into how each installation was performing. Performance issues — degraded panels, failing inverters, battery problems — were only discovered when clients reported power outages. By that point, damage had already occurred and the company's reputation suffered. Remote monitoring existed on some systems but was fragmented across three incompatible manufacturer apps.
